definitions.definition: What is real in the ultimate sense is fourfold: consciousness, mental factors, matter and nibbāna; everything else (persons, things, time, place) is concept.

name: Conventional and ultimate truth (sammuti- and paramattha-sacca)

definitions.definition: The Buddha taught both in conventional terms (persons, beings) and in ultimate terms (aggregates, dhammas); both are true on their own level; the Abhidhamma is teaching in ultimate terms. 'Chariot' is a mere term; ultimately only its parts, and only mentality-materiality, are found.
Conventions (sammuti) must be used and respected, but the heart that has seen through them is released (vimutti) from them.

relations.note: the suttas' use of worldly expressions without misapprehension is systematized by the commentaries as the two truths

definitions.definition: Concepts are twofold — concept as meaning (what is made known) and concept as name (what makes it known); they have no intrinsic nature; the Puggalapaññatti treats persons as such designations.

name: The four defining devices (lakkhaṇa, rasa, paccupaṭṭhāna, padaṭṭhāna)

definitions.definition: The commentaries define each dhamma by its characteristic, function, manifestation and proximate cause.

Twenty-two triads and one hundred Abhidhamma dyads (in clusters: roots, taints, fetters, ties, floods, bonds, hindrances, misapprehension, clinging, defilements) plus forty-two sutta dyads, by which every dhamma is classified; the Paṭṭhāna applies its conditions to the same matrix.

name: The analytical methods of the Abhidhamma books

definitions.definition: Matrix classification (Dhammasaṅgaṇī), analysis by sutta and Abhidhamma methods with a question section (Vibhaṅga), inclusion/association (Dhātukathā), designation of persons (Puggalapaññatti), formal debate (Kathāvatthu), converse pairs (Yamaka) and conditional relations (Paṭṭhāna).

Consciousness is one in its characteristic of knowing but 89 types by plane, kind and association: 54 sense-sphere (12 unwholesome, 18 rootless, 24 beautiful), 15 fine-material, 12 immaterial, 8 supramundane (121 when the supramundane are multiplied by five jhānas).

relations.note: Yoga's citta is one mind-stuff with modifications; the Abhidhamma's citta is a series of momentary consciousnesses of many types

name: The fifty-two mental factors (cetasika)

definitions.definition: Mental factors arising with consciousness: 13 ethically variable (7 universals: contact, feeling, perception, volition, one-pointedness, life faculty, attention; 6 occasionals: applied thought, sustained thought, decision, energy, rapture, desire), 14 unwholesome and 25 beautiful.

members: 14 akusala (moha, ahirika, anottappa, uddhacca, lobha, diṭṭhi, māna, dosa, issā, macchariya, kukkucca, thīna, middha, vicikicchā)

relations.note: feeling, perception and the fifty formations

definitions.definition: Greed, hatred and delusion (unwholesome) and non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion (wholesome or indeterminate) are the roots that give firmness to consciousness.

Eighteen concretely produced (four great elements, five sensitivities, four objective fields, two sex faculties, heart-base, life faculty, nutriment) and ten non-concretely produced (space, two intimations, three mutabilities, four characteristics).

relations.note: the Abhidhamma analyses matter into momentary elements, not into guṇas of a single prakṛti
the analysis of the aggregate of matter

name: The heart-base (hadaya-vatthu)

definitions.definition: Mind-element and mind-consciousness-element occur in dependence on a material base; the canon (Paṭṭhāna) leaves it unnamed and the Dhammasaṅgaṇī does not list it; the commentaries and manuals identify it as the heart, within the blood in the heart cavity.

notes: The Theravāda's only 'seat of mind' teaching; no channel/cakra anatomy is taught in the Abhidhamma (contrast the borān and Dhammakāya bodily bases).

definitions.definition: Matter originates from kamma, consciousness, temperature and nutriment.
Matter occurs in inseparable groups (at least the eight: four elements, colour, odour, flavour, nutritive essence) which arise and cease together.
Seen directly with the light of deep concentration and analysed into their elements before insight.
Their extremely rapid arising and dissolution is felt in meditation as subtle vibration.
Each consciousness has three sub-moments (arising, presence, dissolution); a material phenomenon lasts seventeen mind-moments.

Consciousness occurs in fixed series: the five-door process of up to seventeen mind-moments (life-continuum, adverting, sense consciousness, receiving, investigating, determining, seven impulsions, two registrations), mind-door processes, absorption and path processes; each moment conditions the next by proximity, contiguity, absence and disappearance.
The passive resultant consciousness that flows whenever no active process occurs (as in dreamless sleep), identical in type with the rebirth-linking and death consciousness of that life.

relations.note: Yoga treats deep sleep as a mental modification (nidrā-vṛtti); the Abhidhamma as the uninterrupted life-continuum

definitions.definition: The commentary identifies the luminous mind of AN 1.49–52 with the life-continuum, defiled by adventitious defilements.
The radiant citta known in meditation; defilements are visitors (Ajahn Mun); ignorance can reside in its radiance (Ajahn Maha Boowa).

Four woeful planes (hell, animals, ghosts, asuras), the human realm and six sense-sphere heavens, sixteen fine-material Brahma realms (including the five Pure Abodes and the realm of non-percipient beings) and four immaterial realms; life-spans increase upward.
An eon has four incalculable phases; the world is destroyed in turn by fire (up to the Ābhassara), water (up to the Subhakiṇha) and wind (up to the Vehapphala).

name: Death and rebirth-linking in the Abhidhamma

definitions.definition: Death comes by exhaustion of life-span, of kamma, of both, or by a destructive kamma; at death a kamma, a kamma-sign or a destiny-sign presents itself; death consciousness is followed immediately by rebirth-linking with that object — there is no intermediate existence.

By function (productive, supportive, obstructive, destructive); by order of ripening (weighty, death-proximate, habitual, reserve); by time (here and now, next life, later lives, defunct); by place (unwholesome, sense-sphere wholesome, fine-material, immaterial).

relations.note: Yoga Sūtra 4.7's classes of karma by colour (white, black, both, neither)

definitions.definition: Events are governed by five orders — of temperature/seasons, seeds, kamma, mind, and Dhamma — so not everything experienced is due to kamma.
Expounded at length in Ledi Sayadaw's Niyāma Dīpanī as the cosmic order without a creator.

name: The twenty-four conditions (paccaya) of the Paṭṭhāna

definitions.definition: Root, object, predominance, proximity, contiguity, conascence, mutuality, support, decisive support, prenascence, postnascence, repetition, kamma, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, absence, disappearance, non-disappearance; all reducible to four (object, decisive support, kamma, presence).

name: Dependent origination in the Abhidhamma and commentaries

definitions.definition: Expounded by the sutta method across three lives — three periods, twelve factors, twenty modes, three links, four groups, three rounds (defilement, kamma, result) — and by the Abhidhamma method within a single moment of consciousness; the wheel has no maker and no experiencer.
The whole sequence happens in daily life at each unmindful contact; 'birth' is the birth of the ego.
To be understood intellectually (with a chart) before insight practice.

relations.note: the commentarial and Abhidhamma exposition of the sutta teaching

name: How the Abhidhamma was taught and handed down

definitions.definition: The Buddha taught it in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, gave the method to Sāriputta daily, and Sāriputta taught it; it was recited at the First Council and preserved by reciters; the Kathāvatthu was expanded by Moggaliputta Tissa at the Third Council from the Buddha's outline.

Ten kasiṇas, ten foulnesses, ten recollections, four divine abidings, four formless states, one perception (repulsiveness of nutriment) and one defining (of the four elements); ten lead only to access, thirty to absorption.

relations.note: the Visuddhimagga's subjects of calm versus the sutta frame of mindfulness; several subjects overlap

definitions.definition: Greedy, hating, deluded, faithful, intelligent and speculative; each has suitable subjects, dwellings and postures; faith parallels greed, intelligence hatred, speculation delusion.
The Vimuttimagga counts fourteen kinds of behaviour including mixed types (as reported).

name: The good friend (kalyāṇamitta) as meditation teacher

definitions.definition: The meditation subject is received from a good friend who is lovable, respected, esteemed, able to counsel, patient, able to give deep talk and never urges to what is useless; best is the Buddha, then the great disciples, then an arahant, and so on down to one who knows the texts; a person can be a decisive-support condition.
Close personal training under an experienced forest teacher who knows the pupil's mind.
Formal request of the meditation subject from the teacher with offerings.
Momentary, access and absorption concentration; development proceeds through preliminary work, access and absorption.

relations.note: absorption with a supporting object in the Buddhist and Pātañjala schemes (band B4); a correspondence of position, not of theory
the calm side of calm and insight

definitions.definition: Preliminary sign (the object as first taken up), learning sign (the image seen with eyes closed) and counterpart sign (a purified image born of perception, appearing with access).
Listed by the Visuddhimagga among the three kinds of concentration; the sub-commentary makes momentary unification the concentration of the pure-insight practitioner.
Built up by uninterrupted noting; sufficient to suppress the hindrances and carry insight to the path.

name: The two vehicles: calm-first and pure insight

definitions.definition: One whose vehicle is calm develops jhāna and then insight; one whose vehicle is pure insight (the dry-insight worker) begins with the four elements; both reach the paths, whose jhāna-level is determined by the insight leading to emergence.
Both vehicles require at least access concentration strong enough to see ultimate realities.
The pure-insight vehicle through momentary concentration is fully valid.

name: The fourfold and fivefold jhāna schemes

definitions.definition: The suttas count four jhānas; the Abhidhamma also counts five by separating the removal of applied and of sustained thought; the fifth has only equanimity and one-pointedness.

relations.note: the Abhidhamma's fivefold count of the same absorptions

definitions.definition: Minor, momentary, showering, uplifting and pervading rapture.
Induced one after another at points in the body as the first stage of the old meditation.

Five mundane direct knowledges developed from the fourth jhāna — supernormal powers, the divine ear, knowledge of others' minds, recollection of past lives, the divine eye — and the sixth, supramundane, destruction of the taints; the worldling's powers are fragile and an impediment to insight.

relations.note: both are powers born of concentration and both texts warn that they obstruct the highest aim; the goals (nibbāna / kaivalya) differ

name: The ten kinds of supernormal power

definitions.definition: By resolve, by transformation, mind-made, by intervention of knowledge, by intervention of concentration, the noble power, born of kamma-result, of the meritorious, accomplished by lore, and success through right application.

name: The seven purifications (satta visuddhi)

definitions.definition: Purification of virtue and of mind are the roots; purification of view, by overcoming doubt, by knowledge and vision of path and not-path, of the way, and knowledge and vision are the trunk; the list comes from the Rathavinīta Sutta (MN 24).

notes: The path map itself is pth:seven-purifications (owned by U51).

name: Virtue, concentration, understanding as the frame of the Visuddhimagga

definitions.definition: The Visuddhimagga expounds the whole path through the verse 'established in virtue, developing mind and understanding'.

relations.note: the Visuddhimagga's organization of the path

name: The insight knowledges (vipassanā-ñāṇa)

definitions.definition: The Visuddhimagga's purification by knowledge and vision of the way consists of eight knowledges and conformity; the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha lists ten insight knowledges (adding comprehension); the later tradition counts sixteen by adding the discernment of mentality-materiality, of conditions, change-of-lineage, path, fruit and reviewing.
The stages as they unfold in noting practice, described in The Progress of Insight.

notes: The numbered list of sixteen is later than the Visuddhimagga (correction to the unit brief); path map pth:sixteen-insight-knowledges is owned by U51.

definitions.definition: Full understanding as the known, as investigation, and as abandoning.
The signless, desireless and void gateways, entered through the contemplations of impermanence, suffering and not-self.

name: The four paths and four fruits

definitions.definition: Stream-entry, once-return, non-return and arahantship, each a path moment followed by fruition; the paths abandon the fetters in stages; supramundane consciousness has jhāna character.

notes: The sutta path map is pth:four-stages-of-awakening (owned by U51).

relations.note: path and fruit take nibbāna as object

definitions.definition: After each path and fruit the noble person may review path, fruit, nibbāna, defilements abandoned and those remaining — nineteen kinds in all.
By substitution of opposites (in insight), by suppression (in concentration), by cutting off (in the path), by tranquillization (in fruition), by escape (nibbāna).

name: Nibbāna in the Abhidhamma and commentaries

definitions.definition: The unconditioned element, existing and apprehensible by the path, one in nature, with or without residue, void, signless and desireless; not a self and not a creator.
A realm and true self where the Dhammakāyas abide (contested).
The coolness of extinguished defilements here and now.

relations.note: the Theravāda denies any self in liberation

definitions.definition: The temporary cessation of consciousness and mental factors, attained by non-returners and arahants who have the eight attainments, after preparatory resolutions.

name: Types of person (puggala) in the Abhidhamma

definitions.definition: Persons designated by attainment and disposition: the worldling, the one at change-of-lineage, the trainees, the faith- and Dhamma-followers, the body-witness, the one attained to view, those liberated by faith, by wisdom and both ways, the kinds of stream-enterer and non-returner.
Pali (Māgadhī) is the language of intrinsic nature and the root language of all beings; the analytical knowledge of language recognizes it.
The dispensation disappears in five stages — attainment, practice, learning, signs, relics.

name: Urgency of practice within the dispensation

definitions.definition: Now, while the dispensation lasts, laypeople and monks should develop the requisites of awakening rather than wait for a future Buddha.
The clock of vipassanā has struck: 2,500 years after the Buddha the practice is to spread again (U Ba Khin's account).

name: Meditation and Abhidhamma study by laypeople

definitions.definition: Ledi Sayadaw taught insight and Abhidhamma to laypeople and authorized lay teachers.
Lay teachers (Saya Thetgyi, U Ba Khin, Goenka) and courses open to all.
Retreat centres open to lay meditators under the Buddha Sāsana Nuggaha Organization.
Precise mental labelling of each object as it arises — rising, falling, thinking, hearing — which keeps mindfulness continuous and reveals arising and passing.
Bare attention: registering what happens without reaction or comment (Nyanaponika).

name: Sensation as the root of reaction (Goenka)

definitions.definition: Every contact produces sensation in the body; craving and aversion arise as reactions to it; equanimous awareness of sensations stops new saṅkhāras and lets old ones surface and pass.
The knowing nature of the heart, which observes phenomena; the forest teachers train it but deny that it is a self.

name: The radiant citta as the seat of ignorance

definitions.definition: At the final stage the radiant, seemingly perfect citta is the last hiding place of ignorance and must be seen through (Ajahn Maha Boowa).
A mind void of 'I' and 'mine', working and living without self-grasping; the practical meaning of suññatā.
Terms like birth, rebirth, heaven and hell have an everyday sense and a Dhamma sense referring to present mental states.

relations.note: a hermeneutic of levels of meaning, applied by Buddhadāsa beyond the commentarial use

name: The inner bodies of the Dhammakāya method

definitions.definition: Resting the mind at the centre of the body, the meditator sees a bright sphere and successive refined bodies (human, divine, Brahma, formless Brahma, and the Dhammakāya bodies of the paths), culminating in the Dhammakāya of the arahant.

notes: From secondary knowledge only; no primary text read.
